- Stakeholders we noted: you (product lead), Raj (legal) for contract/DPA, Procurement inbox for purchase order, and the CTO (TBD) as economic approver.

Requests / next steps I have for your team:
1) Can you confirm who will be the final economic buyer (name + title)?
2) Procurement timeline & PO process (standalone or through SOW + PO)?
3) Any specific security questionnaires we should expect beyond SOC2 (e.g., data residency / custom controls)?

I attached a SOC2 snapshot and the latest DPA draft to speed review: [attachment: SOC2-snapshot-2025.pdf] [attachment: Redwood-DPA-v3.docx].

If it helps, Marissa (cc'd) can do a short technical review call with Raj or your security lead next week. I can also start a mutual action plan once you confirm the buyer and procurement cadence.

Thanks, Soojin. Helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Economic buyer will be our VP of Engineering, Marcus Li — I looped Procurement and Raj for next steps.
- Procurement prefers a PO against a master services agreement; timeline is roughly 3–4 weeks once legal signs off.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Amelia

Subject: Fwd: Demo recap + buying path — need quick internal on exceptions

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Amelia's note. Key takeaways that will likely require an internal exception:

- Procurement wants PO against an MSA + DPA (standard).
- They expect an SLA at 99.9% with the possibility of SLA credit language (Amelia may ask for a small credit in the contract).
- They have a security questionnaire coming; Raj will review DPA for redlines.

Question for you both: given this is a mid-size pilot ($~25k/mo) and the economic buyer is Marcus Li, do we have flexibility on: (A) offering a modest introductory discount for a 6-month pilot, and (B) approving SLA credit language beyond our standard terms?

Why I ask: this account is strategically good for us in Healthcare (HIPAA prospect, reference potential). I want to propose either a 10% pilot discount or a capped SLA credit (e.g., credit limited to first month's fee) to keep procurement moving — but I need approval path.

Can we get a quick runbook: who signs off on pricing exceptions under $50k ARR? Who can approve SLA exceptions?

Thanks — Soojin

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Demo recap + buying path — need quick internal on exceptions

Soojin — quick yes with conditions.

- Pricing: You have delegated authority to approve up to 12% discount for pilot deals that are < $50k ARR and tied to a 6-month minimum commitment and a reference agreement. If you use the full 12%, please document justification in the HubSpot deal notes and loop me.
- SLA exceptions: We generally don't change core SLAs. For a limited pilot, approve a capped SLA credit (max = 100% of one month of committed fees) provided legal signs off on indemnity language. Marissa, please confirm technical feasibility for our current hosting profile (region and multi-az).
- Contract: Any DPA redlines that add new data residency requirements must go to the security/compliance review queue; do not sign off on data residency changes without S&C approval.

Please proceed with the PO/MSA track and get Raj's edits. Soojin — once you have Marcus confirmed and procurement timeline, create the MAP and I'll review before you send the exception language to them.

Evelyn Hart
VP Sales | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
